title: OPTICAL BURST SWITCHING IN OPTICAL SATELLITE NETWORKS - EXPRO PLUS
description: "All-Optical" Satellite Networking (OSN) using Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) for theGround-Space, Inter-Satellite and Space-Ground links gains traction with the emergence of relevantcommercial systems and ESA's Hydron proposals. They are based on the concept of "circuit switching" where dedicated optical wavelength channels called "lightpaths" are allocated to a particular connection. Circuit switching is inherently a lower efficiency approach in terms of link-load utilization in exchange for link reliability. Alternative techniques include "packet switching" where each "satellite node" would process "optical packets" instead of "lightpaths". Optical Packetswitching requires some kind of "optical buffering" which is not feasible in practical terms rendering this approach of no practical interest. An intermediate approach is the "optical burst switching" (OBS) which requires no buffering and relies on the use of a dedicated wavelength channel to provide the control commands to the onboard wavelength routers which are reset for a period of time (software-defined network (SDN)). Buffering can take place electronically at the entry/exitnodes (ground or satellites) where the traffic is "sourced" and/or "sunk". This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the status of Packet/Burst Switching in Fiber Optic Networks. Identification of solutions to the buffering issue and explain the applicability of Software Defined Networking;- Analyse the differences in using OBS over an OSN as opposed in-ground networks, in terms of increased delays and more frequent link interruptions, provide a conceptual design of a OBS over the various types of OSN. Assess the potential benefits in terms of link utilization and other network parameters in each type of OSN and provide an SDN-OBS-OSN architecture for further analysis by simulation and laboratory Demonstration;- Simulation of OBS in the selected types of OSN. Measure link utilization, packet loss, delay, etc.- Demonstrate the feasibility of OBS in the selected types of OSN in a laboratory using appropriate equipment to simulate the OSN links;- Conclusions and Recommendations for possible further development.At the end of the activity, a clear picture of the applicability of OBS in WDM OSN is expected tohave been established. In case of positive recommendation, the activity will also provide a roadmap for all the necessary technologies to be developed.

title: DIGITAL TWIN OF A SPACECRAFT AUTONOMOUS AND COLLABORATIVE INTELLIGENT MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM (ARTES AT 4G.050)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, implement and test a smart digital twin that can be used to develop and testautonomous satcom building blocks and their collaborative interactions. Examples of building blocks are the onboard computer and remote terminal unit, software, power management and fault detection, isolation and recovery. The digital twin will enable the exploration of a wide range of innovative solutions for managing single or multiple hardware failures, advanced testing aspects and autonomous systems tosupport controlling the S/C.Targeted Improvements: Enabling intelligent satcom satellites and constellations by creating a digital twin tool for faster, flexible and integrated development and testing of intelligent (autonomous) satcomsystems based on multi-agent architecture, not existing today in Europe.Description: The market is continuously requesting satcom systems to improve in adaptability, resource efficiency, autonomy and fault tolerance. The introduction of intelligent satcom systems has the potential to not only improve the operational efficiency and reliability of the satellite or satellite constellation but also enhanceits ability to perform complex tasks in orbitwith minimal or no intervention from ground. To enable future intelligent satcom constellations, implementation of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) will be pivotal. The decentralised, collaborative nature of MAS allows each system to operate independently, but cooperatively, managing subsystems and components within a satellite, an entire constellation of satellites or even the complete end-to-end satcom system, including the ground segment. This will result in coordinated behaviour,optimal resource utilisation, safereconfigurability, autonomous decision-making among spacecraft, predict and manage overall system/constellation behaviour, identify and resolve potential anomalies, and support mission operations through continuous synchronisation with real-time telemetry data.This activity will develop a satellite digital twin based on a MAS architecture. The digital twin shall be designed to run in parallel with a referenced system development and shall be capable of updating itself using the reference system incoming telemetry. The digital twin shall be a digital model of a reference satellite with a refined digital model of the avionics (OBDH and AOCS/GNC). Other blocks (e.g. power, thermal management) will be modelled at higher, architecture level. The digital twin shall encompass a diagnosticmodule, for health monitoring and prognostics, including analysis of performance drifts, anomalydetection and failure prediction. The digital twin shall track the state of the spacecraft, even in conditions that differ from those anticipated at launch. The digital twin shall predict future behaviour and guide operational decisions with insight into the systems internal dynamics. It shall be able to assist in the evaluation of design and spacecraft configuration choice and trade-offs andperformances.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall include the development of the digital twinconcept and software architecture with a maximum budget range of 1200kE. Phase 1 output will comprise of a digital twin architecture and preliminary digital models of critical avionics blocks.- Phase 2 shall include the full development of digital models of the avionics blocks as well as diagnostic models. The remaining blocks shall be developed at architecture level with critical functions.Phase 2 output will comprise of the digital twin software beta version.

Procedura Tytuł: „Kompleksowy odbiór i zagospodarowanie odpadów komunalnych pochodzących z zamieszkałych i niezamieszkałych nieruchomości na terenie Gminy Drawno w okresie 01.01.2027 r. – 31.12.2027 r.” Opis: 1. Odbiór i zagospodarowanie odpadów komunalnych pozostałych z segregacji (zmieszanych) w okresie 12 miesięcy od właścicieli nieruchomości zamieszkałych i niezamieszkałych na terenie gminy Drawno, w tym również domków letniskowych lub innych nieruchomości wykorzystywanych na cele rekreacyjno-wypoczynkowe, 2. Odbiór i zagospodarowanie frakcji odpadów komunalnych gromadzony w sposób selektywny od właścicieli nieruchomości zamieszkałych i niezamieszkałych na terenie gminy Drawno, w tym również domków letniskowych lub innych nieruchomości wykorzystywanych na cele rekreacyjno-wypoczynkowe, oddzielnie dla: a) papieru i tektury, czasopism, gazet, itp., w tym opakowania; b) szkła i odpadów opakowaniowych ze szkła bezbarwnego i kolorowego; c) tworzyw sztucznych, w tym opakowania i opakowania wielomateriałowe oraz metal; d) odpadów ulegających biodegradacji, bioodpadów, w tym odpady opakowaniowe ulegające biodegradacji i odpady zielone (w tym odbiór choinek). 3. Odbiór i zagospodarowanie pozostałych, powstających na nieruchomościach zamieszkałych odpadów (tzw. zbiórki): a) mebli i innych odpadów wielkogabarytowych; b) zużytego sprzętu elektrycznego i elektronicznego; c) odzieży i tekstyliów; d) zużytych opon. 4. Odbiór i zagospodarowanie odpadów zbieranych w sposób selektywny z Punktu Selektywnego Zbierania Odpadów Komunalnych (PSZOK) w Drawnie, obejmujących następujące frakcje: a) papier, b) szkło, c) metale i tworzywa sztuczne, d) tekstylia, e) odpady wielkogabarytowe, f) zużyte opony, g) sprzęt elektryczny i elektroniczny, źródła światła (żarówki, jarzeniówki itp.), h) baterie i akumulatory, i) odpady niebezpieczne w tym leki i chemikalia pochodzące z gospodarstw domowych, odpady budowlano – remontowe, j) odpady niekwalifikujące się do odpadów medycznych powstałych w gospodarstwie domowym w wyniku przyjmowania produktów leczniczych w formie iniekcji i prowadzenia monitoringu poziomu substancji we krwi, w szczególności igieł i strzykawek. 5. Zakres przedmiotu zamówienia obejmuje transport odebranych odpadów komunalnych do instalacji odzysku i unieszkodliwiania odpadów oraz do instalacji komunalnej. title: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) system and drone
description: Request for tender on InSAR system mounted on Drone Multi-band (P/L/C- band) or at minimum L-band imaging radar will be used for wide-area environmental monitoring. The radar should be mounted on a drone and able to produce single-look complex focused SAR (synthetic aperture radar) images, ground detected images (analysis ready data), and be suitable for interferometric imaging applications. The radar instrumentation and related software should be an actual system proven through successful mission operations in an operational environment. Ready to use product should include all necessary interfaces and software tools for producing analysis ready SAR and InSAR image products with explicit data annotations. The procured system is intended for various environmental monitoring tasks. Delivery six to eight months from contract signing or at the latest by the end of September, 2025. Warranty period minimum one (1) year for InSAR system and drone.
